identity.title: ALMA Sub-arcsecond-resolution 183 GHz H<SUB>2</SUB>O and Dense Molecular Line Observations of Nearby Ultraluminous Infrared Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the results of ALMA $\sim$2 mm, $\lesssim$1$''$-resolution observations of ten (ultra)luminous infrared galaxies (\[U\]LIRGs; infrared luminosity $\gtrsim$ 10$^{11.7}$L$_{\odot}$) at $z <$ 0.15, targeting dense ($>$10$^{4}$ cm$^{-3}$) molecular (HCN, HCO$^{+}$, and HNC J=2–1) and 183 GHz H$_{2}$O 3$_{1,3}$–2$_{2,0}$ emission lines.
We conducted band 5 (163–211 GHz) and 4 (125–163 GHz) observations of nine ULIRGs and one LIRG NGC 1614 (Table 1) in our ALMA Cycle 5 programs 2017.1.00022.S and 2017.1.00023.S (PI = M. Imanishi).

question.value: Investigate the properties of dense molecular gas tracers (HCN, HCO+, and HNC J=2-1) and 183 GHz H2O 3(1,3)-2(2,0) lines in the nuclei of ten nearby (ultra)luminous infrared galaxies with different levels of AGN energetic contributions.

evidence.quote: We conducted ALMA band 4–5 ($\sim$2 mm) observations of nine ultraluminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs; L$_{\rm IR}$ $>$ 10$^{12}$L$_{\odot}$) at $z =$ 0.04–0.14, and one starburst-dominated luminous infrared galaxy, NGC 1614 (LIRG; L$_{\rm IR}$ $=$ 10$^{11.7}$L$_{\odot}$) at $z =$ 0.016, with the aim of investigating the properties of dense molecular gas tracers (HCN, HCO$^{+}$, and HNC J=2–1) and 183 GHz H$_{2}$O 3$_{1,3}$–2$_{2,0}$ lines.

In short, we selected nearby (U)LIRGs that (1) had different levels of AGN’s energetic contributions to the bolometric luminosity, based on optical/infrared/(sub)millimeter spectroscopic energy diagnostic methods and (2) were expected to show bright molecular emission lines, to investigate their flux ratios with small statistical uncertainty.
We conducted band 5 (163–211 GHz) and 4 (125–163 GHz) observations of nine ULIRGs and one LIRG NGC 1614 (Table 1) in our ALMA Cycle 5 programs 2017.1.00022.S and 2017.1.00023.S (PI = M. Imanishi).
This paper made use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00022.S and #2017.1.00023.S.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Widest 1.875 GHz mode with 1920 channels per spw; 4 spws total (2 in each sideband) for J21a and J21b setups; binned by 20 channels (~35 km/s) for ULIRGs and 10 channels (~20 km/s) for NGC 1614

evidence.quote: We employed the widest 1.875 GHz mode with 1920 channels for each spectral window.

We then applied the CASA task “clean” (Briggs weighting; robust $=$ 0.5 and gain $=$ 0.1) to create maps of the continuum-subtracted molecular line data, by binning 20 channels for all ULIRGs (velocity resolution $\sim$ 35 km s$^{-1}$).
For the LIRG NGC 1614, we applied 10 channels binning ($\sim$20 km s$^{-1}$), because molecular emission lines were much narrower than those of other ULIRGs.
Data of dense molecular gas tracers, HCN J=2–1 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 177.261 GHz) and HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 178.375 GHz) lines, were obtained in one observation (called as “J21a”).
Data of dense molecular gas tracers, HCN J=2–1 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 177.261 GHz) and HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 178.375 GHz) lines, were obtained in one observation (called as “J21a”).
Data of HNC J=2–1 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 181.325 GHz) and 3$_{1,3}$–2$_{2,0}$ line of para-H$_{2}$O at $\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 183.310 GHz (183 GHz H$_{2}$O) were obtained separately (“J21b”).
Data of HNC J=2–1 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 181.325 GHz) and 3$_{1,3}$–2$_{2,0}$ line of para-H$_{2}$O at $\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 183.310 GHz (183 GHz H$_{2}$O) were obtained separately (“J21b”).

The vibrationally excited v$_{2}$=1, l=1f (v$_{2}$=1f) HCN (hereafter HCN-VIB) J=2–1 line at $\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 178.136 GHz and vibrationally excited v$_{2}$=1f HCO$^{+}$ (HCO$^{+}$-VIB) J=2–1 line at $\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 179.129 GHz were also included in this sideband.

The vibrationally excited v$_{2}$=1, l=1f (v$_{2}$=1f) HCN (hereafter HCN-VIB) J=2–1 line at $\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 178.136 GHz and vibrationally excited v$_{2}$=1f HCO$^{+}$ (HCO$^{+}$-VIB) J=2–1 line at $\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 179.129 GHz were also included in this sideband.

For the J21b observations, we covered the HNC J=2–1 and 183 GHz H$_{2}$O lines and vibrationally excited v$_{2}$=1f HNC (HNC-VIB) J=2–1 line at $\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 182.584 GHz in two spectral windows on one sideband, and used two additional spectral windows in another sideband.

The HC$_{3}$N J=20–19 line at $\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 181.945 GHz was covered in the J21b spectra of all ten (U)LIRGs and was clearly detected in four ULIRGs (IRAS 12112$+$0305 NE, IRAS 15250$+$3609, IRAS 20551$-$4250, and IRAS 22491$–$1808 in Figure 3f, 3n, 3r, and 3t, respectively).

In the spectrum of IRAS 20551–4250 (Figures 3q and 3u), at the high frequency side of the HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 line, an emission line signature exists, which we identify as SO 5(4)–4(3) ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 178.605 GHz).
Moreover, the HOC$^{+}$ J=2–1 emission line ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 178.972 GHz) is detected (Figure 3u).

In spectral windows other than J21a and J21b, the CS J=4–3 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 195.954 GHz) and HC$_{3}$N J=21–20 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 191.040 GHz) lines are included in certain fraction of (U)LIRGs and are detected in a few (U)LIRGs.

In spectral windows other than J21a and J21b, the CS J=4–3 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 195.954 GHz) and HC$_{3}$N J=21–20 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 191.040 GHz) lines are included in certain fraction of (U)LIRGs and are detected in a few (U)LIRGs.

analysis_steps.goal: Create moment 0, 1, and 2 maps and measure deconvolved emission sizes

method.value: Integrate signals in channels with significant line detection to create moment 0, moment 1, and moment 2 maps at original beam resolution, and measure deconvolved intrinsic emission sizes on moment 0 and continuum maps using CASA task imfit.

evidence.quote: Integrated intensity (moment 0) maps of the HCN J=2–1, HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1, HNC J=2–1 and 183 GHz H$_{2}$O lines are created by integrating signals in channels with significant line detection, and the peak emission flux as well as detection significance is tabulated in Table 4.

Figure 4 shows the intensity-weighted mean velocity (moment 1) maps of the HCN J=2–1, HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1, HNC J=2–1, and 183 GHz H$_{2}$O emission lines whenever they are detected with significantly high S/N ratios to obtain meaningful velocity information (Table 4).
We also (3) compare the measured emission size of the H$_{2}$O with those of other dense molecular gas tracers, by applying the CASA task “imfit” to the original beam moment 0 maps (Figure 1).

evidence.quote: We find that the flux increase from $\sim$1 kpc to 2kpc-beam data, is as high as $\sim$80% in the starburst-dominated ULIRG IRAS 13509$+$0442, but significantly smaller in the remaining ULIRGs (Appendix B).

analysis_steps.goal: Fit Gaussian profiles to spectral lines and compute line flux ratios

method.value: Fit single or double Gaussian profiles to extracted spectra at original, ~1 kpc, 2 kpc, and 200 pc beams to measure velocity-integrated fluxes, and calculate flux ratios among HCN, HCO+, HNC J=2-1, 183 GHz H2O, HC3N, and CS lines.

evidence.quote: Gaussian fits are applied to estimate the molecular emission line flux from nuclear $\sim$1 kpc regions in individual (U)LIRGs (and 200 pc regions for NGC 1614).

However, some molecular emission lines in certain ULIRGs display double-peaked profiles with central dips and clearly deviate from a single Gaussian profile (e.g., HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 line of IRAS 12112$+$0305 NE in Figure 3e). For these, we apply two Gaussian fits (two emission components).

fitting.value: Single or double Gaussian profile fitting (fixing peak or FWHM to best-fit value when needed for faint/blended lines)

evidence.quote: We apply a single Gaussian fit as long as the observed emission line profile is approximated by a single peaked profile with small deviation.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive line luminosities, nuclear dense molecular gas masses, and gas depletion times

method.value: Convert ~1kpc-beam velocity-integrated line fluxes to L_line (L_sun) and L'_line (K km s^-1 pc^2) using Solomon & Vanden Bout (2005) equations, derive dense gas mass M_dense from HCO+ J=2-1 luminosity, and compute lower limits on gas depletion time t_dep = M_dense / SFR.

evidence.loc: Summary of the 183 GHz H$_{2}$O Emission
evidence.quote: The detection rate of very luminous AGN-origin megamaser 183 GHz H$_{2}$O emission is low (1/8 = 12.5%).

findings_qualitative.value: Higher HCN to HCO+ J=2-1 flux ratios are observed in several, but not all, AGN-important ULIRGs compared to starburst-classified nuclei.

evidence.quote: Higher HCN to HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 flux ratios are observed in some, but not all, AGN-important ULIRGs than in starburst-classified sources.

findings_qualitative.value: 183 GHz H2O emission is detected in almost all AGN-important ULIRGs, but except for the Superantennae, it largely originates from the entire nuclear region (~1 kpc) rather than a compact (<<1 kpc) AGN megamaser.

evidence.quote: We detect 183 GHz H$_{2}$O emission in almost all AGN-important ULIRGs, and elevated H$_{2}$O emission is found in two sources with elevated HCN J=2–1 emission, relative to HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1. Except one ULIRG (the Superantennae), the H$_{2}$O emission largely comes from the entire nuclear regions ($\sim$1 kpc), rather than AGN-origin megamaser at the very center ($<<$1 kpc).

findings_qualitative.value: Vibrationally excited HCN and HNC J=2-1 lines are detected in a few (U)LIRGs while HCO+-VIB J=2-1 is undetected in all, suggesting HCO+ and HNC are substantially less abundant than HCN in the innermost mid-infrared-irradiated regions.

evidence.quote: Vibrationally excited J=2–1 emission lines of HCN and HNC are detected in a few (U)LIRGs, but those of HCO$^{+}$ are not. It is suggested that in mid-infrared-radiation-exposed innermost regions around energy sources, HCO$^{+}$ and HNC are substantially less abundant than HCN.

findings_qualitative.value: Two serendipitous ~2 mm continuum sources are detected within ~10'' of the target ULIRGs, interpreted as an infrared luminous dusty galaxy at z > 1 (near IRAS 13509+0442) and a blazar (near the Superantennae).

evidence.quote: In our ALMA $\sim$2 mm data of ten (U)LIRGs, two continuum sources are serendipitously detected within $\sim$10$''$, which are likely to be an infrared luminous dusty galaxy at $z >$ 1 and a blazar.

claims.hypothesis: AGN-important ULIRGs exhibit elevated HCN J=2-1 to HCO+ J=2-1 flux ratios compared to starburst-dominated (U)LIRG nuclei, similar to trends seen in J=1-0, J=3-2, and J=4-3 transitions.
claims.experiment: Measure velocity-integrated HCN J=2-1 and HCO+ J=2-1 fluxes in ~1 kpc beam ALMA spectra across eight AGN-important ULIRG nuclei and three starburst-classified nuclei.
claims.result: Four AGN-important ULIRGs (IRAS 12112+0305 NE, IRAS 15250+3609, Superantennae, IRAS 22491-1808) show HCN/HCO+ J=2-1 > 1, whereas four other AGN-important ULIRGs and all three starburst nuclei show HCO+ >= HCN.
claims.finding: Significantly higher HCN to HCO+ J=2-1 flux ratios occur in a high fraction of, but not all, AGN-important ULIRGs compared to starburst-classified sources.

evidence.loc: HCN to HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 Flux Ratios
evidence.quote: From Table 6, we find that the observed HCN J=2–1 flux is significantly higher than the HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 flux in several ULIRGs classified as AGN important ($\S$2; IRAS 12112$+$0305 NE, IRAS 15250$+$3609, the Superantennae, and IRAS 22491$-$1808), while no such trend is seen in the three starbust-classified galaxy nuclei, NGC 1614, IRAS 12112$+$0305 SW, and IRAS 13509$+$0442 ($\S$2), where the observed HCO$^{+}$ flux is higher than or at least comparable to the observed HCN J=2–1 flux.

evidence.loc: HCN to HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 Flux Ratios
evidence.quote: However, not all AGN-important ULIRGs clearly show elevated HCN J=2–1 emission, relative to HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 (e.g., IRAS 06035$-$7102, IRAS 08572$+$3915, IRAS 12127$-$1412, and IRAS 20551$-$4250 in Table 6), as previously seen at other J-transition lines (cite: ima19; pri20).

claims.hypothesis: Luminous 183 GHz H2O emission in AGN-hosting ULIRGs originates primarily from compact (<<1 kpc) AGN-illuminated megamaser emission at the very center of the galaxy nucleus.
claims.experiment: Compare 183 GHz H2O fluxes, multi-aperture (~original, ~1 kpc, 2 kpc) growth curves, imfit deconvolved sizes, H2O/HCO+ ratio maps, and moment 1/2 kinematics against HCN, HCO+, and HNC J=2-1.
claims.result: 183 GHz H2O is detected (>4.5sigma in moment 0) in all AGN-important ULIRGs and is elevated in the Superantennae and IRAS 15250+3609, and shows some compact component in three ULIRGs, but only the Superantennae (1/8 = 12.5%) is dominated by compact AGN megamaser emission.
claims.finding: Except for the Superantennae, the bulk of the 183 GHz H2O emission in ULIRGs comes from the entire nuclear region (~1 kpc) rather than a compact AGN megamaser.

evidence.loc: Summary of the 183 GHz H$_{2}$O Emission
evidence.quote: Except the Superantennae, the bulk of the observed 183 GHz H$_{2}$O luminosity comes from entire nuclear regions ($\sim$1 kpc), most likely thermal emission or possibly ensemble of stellar maser emission (cite: kon17).

evidence.loc: Summary of the 183 GHz H$_{2}$O Emission
evidence.quote: Among ten observed (U)LIRGs, eight ULIRGs are diagnosed to contain luminous obscured AGNs ($\S$2). The detection rate of very luminous AGN-origin megamaser 183 GHz H$_{2}$O emission is low (1/8 = 12.5%).

claims.hypothesis: The bulk of nuclear (~1 kpc) dense molecular gas in merging (U)LIRGs is not forming stars on a free-fall timescale.
claims.experiment: Derive nuclear dense molecular gas mass M_dense from HCO+ J=2-1 luminosity (using alpha_HCO+ = 2-5 M_sun [K km s^-1 pc^2]^-1) and compare the star-formation depletion time t_dep = M_dense/SFR with the free-fall time t_ff of >10^4 cm^-3 gas.
claims.result: Nuclear dense gas masses are >= a few x 10^8 M_sun (1-22 x 10^8 M_sun) and the lower limit on t_dep is ~1-3 x 10^6 yr, which exceeds t_ff <= 5 x 10^5 yr.
claims.finding: Even in (U)LIRGs' compact nuclei where dense gas is highly concentrated, the bulk (>=50%) of dense molecular gas is not forming stars on a free-fall timescale.

evidence.loc: Emission Line Luminosity and Nuclear Dense Molecular Gas Mass
evidence.quote: The estimated lower limit of the depletion time (t$_{\rm dep}$ $\equiv$ M$_{\rm dense}$/SFR) is $\sim$1–3 $\times$ 10$^{6}$ yr, which is shorter than that derived in dense molecular clouds in our Galaxy and nearby star-forming galaxies, $\sim$10$^{7-8}$ yr (cite: lad10; zha14; liu16; tan18; jia20), but it is longer than the free-fall time of dense ($>$10$^{4}$ cm$^{-3}$) molecular gas, t$_{ff}$ $\equiv$ $\sqrt{\frac{3\pi}{32G\rho}}$ $\lesssim$ 5 $\times$ 10$^{5}$ yr (G is the gravitational constant and $\rho$ is the mass volume density).

evidence.loc: Emission Line Luminosity and Nuclear Dense Molecular Gas Mass
evidence.quote: Thus, even considering only for (U)LIRGs’ nuclei where dense molecular gas highly concentrates through galaxy mergers, it is suggested that the bulk ($\gtrsim$50%) of dense molecular gas is not forming stars with a free-fall time scale (cite: kru07), possibly because of various feedback processes from AGN and starburst activities (cite: hop11; hop13; che20).

claims.hypothesis: In the innermost mid-infrared-irradiated obscuring material around luminous energy sources in (U)LIRGs, HCO+ and HNC are substantially less abundant than HCN.
claims.experiment: Search for vibrationally excited v2=1f J=2-1 emission lines of HCN, HCO+, and HNC in the ALMA spectra and moment 0 maps and compare with expected mid-infrared radiative pumping rates.
claims.result: HCN-VIB J=2-1 signatures are detected in four ULIRGs and HNC-VIB J=2-1 in three (U)LIRGs (fainter than expected if abundances were equal), while HCO+-VIB J=2-1 is not detected in any source.
claims.finding: HCO+ and HNC abundances are substantially depressed relative to HCN in the innermost mid-infrared-illuminated warm molecular gas around the luminous AGNs.

evidence.quote: A plausible explanation for the observed weaker-than-expected HNC-VIB emission is that an HNC abundance is depressed substantially in the mid-infrared-radiation-illuminated, innermost high-temperature molecular gas around the luminous energy sources in (U)LIRGs.

The considerably weaker HCO$^{+}$-VIB emission than HCN-VIB in (U)LIRGs is also very difficult to explain unless the HCO$^{+}$ abundance is substantially lower than HCN at the innermost mid-infrared-radiation-illuminated region around the luminous AGNs at the very center of galaxy nuclei (cite: mal96; pap07; har10).

why_this_data.value: Submillimeter/millimeter wavelengths suffer <=1/20 the dust extinction of hard X-rays and mid-IR; ALMA Band 4/5 covers HCN, HCO+, HNC J=2-1 (lower excitation than J=3-2/4-3) and 183 GHz H2O simultaneously at sub-arcsecond (<~1 kpc) resolution for z > 0.02 (U)LIRGs where J=1-0 is redshifted below Band 3.

evidence.quote: (Sub)millimeter at 0.8–3.5 mm is one such wavelengths, with $\lesssim$1/20 extinction effects than hard X-rays at $\sim$10 keV and infrared $\sim$20 $\mu$m (cite: hil83).

Because the excitation energy level is lower at J=2 than at J=3 or J=4, we can (1) discuss dense molecular line flux ratios at J=2–1 less affected by uncertainty of excitation conditions than at J=3–2 and J=4–3, and (2) J=2–1 lines of HCN, HCO$^{+}$, and HNC may be more reliable dense molecular gas mass tracers,

Although sensitive observations of the 183 GHz H$_{2}$O lines are difficult for very nearby sources at $z \sim$ 0 owing to the poor atmospheric transmission of Earth at $\sim$183 GHz, we can observe this line without severe Earth’s atmospheric H$_{2}$O absorption for (U)LIRGs at $z >$ 0.02, rendering this H$_{2}$O line as another potentially good AGN indicator.

why_this_method.value: Smoothing cubes to a matched ~1 kpc physical beam enables direct comparison across galaxies at different redshifts while isolating energetically dominant nuclei from extended (>a few kpc) host-galaxy starbursts; HCO+ J=2-1 is used for dense gas mass because its L_IR slope is closest to unity and it is less biased by AGN chemistry.

evidence.quote: Since probed physical scale in the original beam spectra is largely different among different (U)LIRGs (Table 3), we compare molecular emission line fluxes with the same physical scale for further discussion. We choose 1 kpc, because we can investigate dense molecular emission line properties at energetically dominant ULIRGs’ nuclei (cite: soi00; dia10; ima11; per21), with minimum contaminations from spatially extended ($\gtrsim$a few kpc) star-formation in the host galaxies.

evidence.loc: Emission Line Luminosity and Nuclear Dense Molecular Gas Mass
evidence.quote: We derive nuclear dense molecular gas mass from HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 luminosity, because (1) the slope of infrared and HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 luminosity relation is the closest to unity among the four lines (Figure 9), and (2) HCO$^{+}$ can be a less biased dense molecular gas mass tracer than HCN and HNC, particularly in the vicinity of a luminous AGN (cite: ima20).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using a single Gaussian fit vs. two Gaussian fits for double-peaked emission lines with central dips: adopted two Gaussian fits when they better trace the profile.

evidence.quote: However, some molecular emission lines in certain ULIRGs display double-peaked profiles with central dips and clearly deviate from a single Gaussian profile (e.g., HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 line of IRAS 12112$+$0305 NE in Figure 3e). For these, we apply two Gaussian fits (two emission components).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Explaining the smaller flux increase of H2O vs HNC J=2-1 from original to ~1 kpc beam solely by compact H2O emission vs. central suppression of HNC abundance: tested by comparing H2O with HCN and HCO+ J=2-1 from ~1 kpc to 2 kpc beam.

evidence.quote: However, as HNC abundance can be low in AGN-illuminated warm molecular gas at the center of a galaxy nucleus (cite: ima20), it may be possible that the observed higher HNC J=2–1 flux increase is simply due to the suppression of HNC J=2–1 emission at the innermost region, rather than the presence of compact H$_{2}$O emission. To overcome this ambiguity, we combine the H$_{2}$O data with the HCN and HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 line data as well (different synthesized beams from H$_{2}$O)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Identifying the 156.34 GHz line in the serendipitous northern source of IRAS 13509+0442 as CO J=2-1 at z ~ 0.47: rejected in favor of higher-J CO (J=3-2 to 6-5 at z = 1-4) due to non-detection of CO J=3-2 and 4-3 in Band 6/7 and lack of optical/NIR counterparts.

evidence.quote: If we assume that this emission line signature originates from a bright CO J=2–1 ($\nu_{\rm rest}$ = 230.538 GHz) line, then the redshift of this source becomes $z \sim$ 0.47.
The non-detection of optical and near-infrared counterparts at the position of this northern continuum source (cite: kim02; ima18b) also makes it unlikely that this source is only at $z \sim$ 0.47.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Comparing ~1 kpc and 2 kpc beam spectra showed that most ULIRGs have small flux increases beyond ~1 kpc, whereas increasing the beam size further adds substantial noise and hampers faint line detection.

evidence.quote: Namely, we recover the bulk of ULIRGs’ nuclear dense molecular and 183 GHz H$_{2}$O line emission in the $\sim$1kpc-beam data. A further increase of the beam size does not significantly increase dense molecular emission line signals, but increases noise a lot, making the detection of faint emission lines difficult.

limitations_admitted.value: The sample of ten (U)LIRGs is neither statistically unbiased nor complete.

evidence.quote: Although our sample is not statistically unbiased, nor complete, it can provide useful information on the possible variation of molecular line flux ratios, depending on different AGN’s energetic contributions.

limitations_admitted.value: One sideband in some Band 5 observations fell into the 182-184.5 GHz terrestrial H2O atmospheric absorption band and was completely flagged by the pipeline.

evidence.quote: Although the targeted molecular lines of our sources were confirmed to be not strongly affected by the Earth’s atmospheric absorption, the other sideband in some sources fell into the frequency of low Earth’s atmospheric transmission. These data were completely flagged by ALMA pipeline processes and not used for our analysis.

limitations_admitted.value: Deconvolved intrinsic sizes from imfit cannot be reliably constrained when emission is a factor of >>2-3 smaller than the synthesized beam, or when S/N is limited.

evidence.quote: Because it is very difficult to constrain the deconvolved intrinsic size to be considerably (a factor of $>>$2–3) smaller than the beam size (Table 3, column 6), in the case of extremely compact emission, the derived value can still be larger than the actual value.

limitations_admitted.value: Outer regions of 183 GHz H2O emission are not sufficiently probed in moment 1 maps due to fainter H2O flux compared to HCN, HCO+, and HNC.

evidence.quote: However, since H$_{2}$O emission is fainter than the other dense molecular lines and outer regions are not sufficiently probed in the moment 1 maps (Figure 4), further discussion of the possible dynamical difference is difficult.

limitations_admitted.value: HCN-VIB J=2-1 fluxes in IRAS 12112+0305 NE and IRAS 22491-1808 are only approximate due to blending with the nearby bright HCO+ J=2-1 line.

evidence.quote: These values are only approximate for the HCN-VIB J=2–1 emission line flux, because we choose the integrated frequency range to minimize the contaminations from the nearby bright HCO$^{+}$ J=2–1 emission line

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-transition (J=2-1) line ratios cannot uniquely separate chemical abundance variations from excitation/density effects without multi-transition non-LTE radiative transfer modeling (deferred to a companion paper).

Infrared luminosities used to compute star-formation rates and gas depletion times are measured from large (>30'') IRAS apertures and include unknown fractional AGN contributions, making SFR and t_dep comparison with 1 kpc ALMA beams systematically uncertain.

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA project codes 2017.1.00022.S and 2017.1.00023.S are stated in the text and Acknowledgments.

evidence.quote: This paper made use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00022.S and #2017.1.00023.S.

missing_for_reproduction: Exact CASA and ALMA pipeline versions
CASA clean stopping threshold, niter, and clean mask definitions
Exact channel/frequency integration windows used for moment 0, 1, and 2 maps of each line and target
Exact pixel size used for each individual target image cube
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~50-150 GB (26 execution blocks across 10 targets in Band 4 and Band 5, 4 spectral windows of 1920 channels each)
reproducibility.score_reason: Observing log, calibrators, continuum frequency windows, weighting (Briggs robust=0.5), channel binning, smoothed physical beam sizes, peak coordinates, and Gaussian fit parameters are all thoroughly tabulated; minor imaging and moment-integration parameters (exact velocity windows, clean thresholds, CASA version) are omitted.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Both ALMA Cycle 5 datasets (2017.1.00022.S and 2017.1.00023.S) are public in the ALMA archive, the data reduction uses standard pipeline calibration plus straightforward CASA tasks (uvcontsub, clean, imsmooth, imfit), and all intermediate and final numeric measurements (continuum fluxes, Gaussian line fits at multiple physical apertures, deconvolved sizes, luminosities, and gas masses) are comprehensively tabulated.

methods_papers.why: Standard formulas for converting molecular line velocity-integrated flux to line luminosities L_line and L'_line
Conversion factor from optically thick HCO+ J=1-0 luminosity to dense H2 molecular gas mass
Calibration of star formation rate from infrared luminosity

companion_papers.why: Prior ALMA Band 6/7 observations of J=3-2 and J=4-3 HCN, HCO+, and HNC lines for the same sample of ten (U)LIRGs
Previously published detailed study of the 183 GHz H2O megamaser emission in one of the sample targets, the Superantennae
Planned paper compiling J=2-1, J=3-2, and J=4-3 HCN, HCO+, and HNC data with non-LTE radiative transfer modeling
